events.title: Joshua Takes Leadership
events.description: After Moses' death, God speaks to Joshua and commands him to lead the people across the Jordan into the Promised Land. God promises to be with him just as He was with Moses.

events.title: Rahab and the Spies
events.description: Joshua sends two spies to Jericho. The prostitute Rahab hides them and helps them escape. In return, they promise to spare her and her family when the city is captured.

events.title: Crossing of the Jordan
events.description: The priests carry the ark of the covenant into the Jordan River, and the water stops flowing so that the entire people can cross on dry ground. Twelve stones are set up as a memorial at Gilgal.

events.title: Circumcision at Gilgal
events.description: Joshua circumcises the new generation of Israelites at Gilgal. God says He has rolled away the disgrace of Egypt from them. They celebrate Passover, and the manna ceases.

events.title: The Commander of the Lord's Army
events.description: Joshua meets a man with a drawn sword outside Jericho who reveals himself as the commander of the Lord's army. Joshua falls on his face and worships.

events.title: The Fall of Jericho
events.description: Israel marches around Jericho for seven days in obedience to God's command. On the seventh day, the walls fall after the people blow trumpets and shout. Rahab and her family are spared.

events.title: Defeat at Ai and Achan's Sin
events.description: Israel suffers defeat at Ai because Achan has taken some of the devoted things from Jericho. Achan is exposed, confesses, and is stoned along with his entire family in the Valley of Achor.

events.title: Victory over Ai
events.description: God gives Joshua a new strategy with an ambush. Israel lures the army out of Ai and captures the city. Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal and reads the law to all the people.

events.title: The Gibeonites' Deceit
events.description: The Gibeonites trick Israel into making a covenant by pretending to come from a distant land. When the deception is discovered, Israel must keep the covenant but makes them woodcutters and water carriers.

events.title: The Sun Stands Still
events.description: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon. Joshua comes to their aid, and God hurls large hailstones upon the enemy. Joshua commands the sun to stand still over Gibeon, and the day is extended until Israel achieves victory.

events.title: Conquest of the South
events.description: Joshua pursues the five kings and executes them. He then captures the cities in southern Canaan: Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, and Debir.

events.title: Conquest of the North
events.description: King Jabin of Hazor gathers a large alliance against Israel. Joshua attacks them at the waters of Merom and defeats them. He captures Hazor and all the northern cities.

events.title: Summary of Conquered Kings
events.description: A complete list of the 31 kings that Israel defeated, both east of the Jordan under Moses and west of the Jordan under Joshua.

events.title: The Land Distribution Begins
events.description: The land is distributed among the nine and a half tribes by casting lots at Shiloh. Caleb receives Hebron as his inheritance after having been a faithful spy. Each tribe receives its territory.

events.title: Cities of Refuge
events.description: Six cities of refuge are designated where someone who unintentionally kills another may seek protection: Kedesh, Shechem, and Hebron west of the Jordan, and Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan east of the Jordan.

events.title: Joshua's Farewell Speech and Covenant Renewal at Shechem
events.description: Joshua gathers all the tribes at Shechem and delivers his farewell speech. He recounts God's deeds from Abraham to the conquest and challenges the people: "Choose today whom you will serve!" The people renew their covenant with the Lord.

events.title: The Death of Joshua
events.description: Joshua dies at the age of 110 and is buried in Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. The Israelites served the Lord as long as Joshua lived, and as long as the elders who had witnessed all that God had done for them were alive.
